chapter: Liberty Band, marriage and the Depression
title: Bands after Red Island and through the Depression
summary: After leaving Red Island he stayed with 'that day' about four years, then worked with a curtain man, John Cavan and Wooden Joe through the Depression.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: The Depression years and the WPA band

blocks.x: Ask him who you played with after you left Red Island.
He said, who did you play with after you left Red Island?
I stayed with that day about four years. Then after that I went with different bands, you know, but they didn't keep up long, you know.
Ask him who you was playing with when depression came on.

You say, who was you playing with when depression came on? Depression. Depression. Depression. Depression. Depression. Yeah. What is that, depression? Tough times. When it was so tough, hard and tough to get along. Oh.

I was with, let me see. I was with my wife's curtain. When it's poor, you got in there. I was with him. Then there, that. He lost that job. He wasn't paying but a dime a quarter of a night. He lost that. Then I went back with John Cavan. He stayed with John Cavan for about three years. And John, when the stick came up a little bit, John wouldn't ask the boys for a raise. That's Bill Key's bad enough, you see. Then I went from different fellas, you know. They hired me, you know. Wooden Joe. You got any name Wooden Joe? And his nephew, Albert Nickerson? Yeah, he was a good sacrifice man.
